BENNETT, MAURICE CHRISTMAS, F.S.I.—Served in Great War, 1914-19; ment. in desps.; capt., R. of O.; joined O.E.T.A., Nov., 1918; absorbed in civil adminstr., Palestine, as asst. dir., grade F, dept., lands and surveys, July, 1920.

BENNETT, Rt. Hon. RICHARD BEDFORD, P.C. (1930). P.C. (Can.), LL.B., K.C.—B. 1870; ed. pub. and high schls., N.B., Dalhousie Univ., N.S.; hon. degree L.L.D., Dalhousie Univ., Queen's Univ. and Univ. of Alberta; admitted to bar of N.B., 1903; mem., legis. assem., Northwest Territories, 1898-1905; legis. assem. of Alta., 1909; rep. Calgary in H. of C., Canada, 1911-17; min. of just. and atty.-gen., 1921; min. of finance in Meighen adminstr., 1926; leader of conserv. party, Oct., 1927; prime min. of Canada after g.e., June, 1930; leader of opposition, 1936-38.

BENNETTS, ALBERT THOMAS, A.C.S.M., M.A.I.M.E., M.A.I.M.M.—B.1890; ed. Camborne Schl. of Mines, 1908-11; medallist of the Royal Cornwall Polytechnic Soc'y., 1910; 1st cls. hons. and silver medallist, City and Guilds of London Inst., 1911; 1st cls. diploma, Camborne Schl. of Mines, 1911; mines dept., F.M.S., 1912-25; asst. ward., mines, Perak, Nov., 1929; senr. inspr., mines, Jan., 1931; asst. ward., mines, Selangor, Mar., 1932; as. ward., mines, Pahang, May, 1932; do., Selangor and N. Sembilan, Sept., 1935; do., Pahang, Jan., 1936 and Oct., 1937;
senr. inspr. of mines, Selangor and N. Sembilan, Apr., 1938; ag. do., Perak, Jan., 1939.

BENSON, GEORGE ALLEN RALSTON.—B. 1879; 6th cls. offr., cust., Br. Guiana, 1901; 5th cls., 1904; 4th cls., 1911; 3rd cls., 1915; 2nd cls., 1924; 1st cls., 1925; ast. survr., enst., 1926; survr., cust., B. Guiana, 1927.

BENSON, SIR J. HAWTREY, KT. BACH. (1912), A.B., M.D., F.R.C.P. Irel.—Ed. Trin. Coll., Dublin; 1st hon. maths., graduated, 1864; consulting physician to Royal City of Dublin Hosp., and to the Monkstown Hosp. Fellow of Acad. of Med., Ireland; late censor and examr., Royal Coll. of Phys., Ireland, and late external examr. in med., Dub. Univ.; is now med. advsr. for Ireland to C.O.; author of numerous papers and articles on technical med. subjects; ret., 1926.

BENTINCK, LILLIE JOSEPHINE, M.B., B.Ch., certif. L.S.T.M.—Lady med. offr., B. Gajah, May, 1921; Ipoh, July, 1921; K. Pahang, July, 1923; Taiping, Apr., 1925; K. Kangsar, June, 1925; lady med. offr., infant welfare centre, Taiping, Aug., 1925; Seremban, July, 1926; K. Lumpur, Sept., 1927; Ipoh, Nov., 1927; K. Kangsar, Feb., 1937.

BENTINCK, MAJOR WALTER GUY, BARON, C.M.G. (1912), D.S.O. (1902).—Ed. at Marlborough Coll., Jena Univ., Germany, and Royal Mil. Coll., Sandhurst; joined Rifle Brig., 1885; capt., 1894; major, 1902; ret., 1905; intelligence dept., W.O., 1899; served throughout S. African war, 1899-1902; (ment. in despatches, Queen's medal with six clasps, King's medal with two clasps); dist. comsnr., Vereeniging, 1900; res. mag., Wakkerstroom dist., Transvaal, 1901-1907; Transvaal mem. of Natal-Transvaal boundary comn., 1902; sec. in office of high comn. for S. Africa, 1907; ag. Imperial soc., Aug., 1907, to Mar., 1908; ast. Imperial soc., Apr., 1908; chmn. Swaziland water comn., 1909.

BENZIES, DOUGLAS, M.A., B.Sc.—B. 1899; ed. Heriot's Sch., Edinburgh; Edin. Univ., 1919-25; M.A., B.Sc.; France, June-Dec., 1918; demob., Jan., 1919; ast. mast., Achimota, Gold Coast, 1925.

BERENDSEN, CARL AUGUST, C.M.G. (1936), LL.M.—B. 1890; ed. Australian pub. schls., Gore Dist. High Schl. (N.Z.) and Victoria Univ. Coll.; entd. N.Z. educ. dept., 1906; lab. dept., 1916; chf. clk., 1917; dep. regist., industrial unions, 1919; Imperial affrs. offr., prime min.'s dept., 1926; perm. head, prime min.'s dept., 1933; also sec. for external affrs., from 1928; mem., N.Z. deleg. to L. of N. assembly, 1936; N.Z. deleg. to Imp. Conf., 1937.

BERNARD, ALBERT VICTOR, O.B.E. (1928), M.D. (Malta), D.P.H. (L'pool), D.T.M. & H. (Engl.), Hon. Assoc., Ord. of St. John, Offr. Ord. Crown of Italy.—B. 1885; ast. res. M.O., Malta gvt. hosp., 1909; M.O.H., 1912; prof. hyg. and prev. med., Malta Univ., 1921; ast. supt., pub. hith., 1929; chf. gvt. med. offr., 1936; temp. offl. mem., coun. of gvt., 1918 & 1921; mem. gen. coun., Malta Univ.; ag. rector, 1935-36.

BERNARD, ANDREW JOSEPH—B. 1892; ed. St. Mary's Coll., Trinidad, Ushaw Coll., Durham and St. Edmund's Coll., Herts.; Trinidad civ. serv., 1911; war serv., 1915-19; ast. warden, Caroni, Jan., 1930; do., St. Pat., 1930; senr. do., Victoria, Jan., 1935; warden, Caroni, Aug., 1938.

BERNARD, LIEUT.-GEN. SIR DENIS KIRWAN K.C.B., 1939, C.B., 1935, C.M.G., 1918, D.S.O., 1917.—B. 1882; ed. Eton and Sandhurst; 2nd lt., Rifle Brig., 1902; capt., 1912; served European War (France, Gallipoli, Salonica and Egypt), 1914-18 (despatches, C.M.G., D.S.O., bt. major, bt. lt.-col., Croix-de-Guerre); G.S.O., Mar., 1915 till end of war; brevet-col., 1923; lt.-col., 1927; col., 1930; major-gen., 1933; commanded 1st Batt. Royal Ulster Rifles, 1927-30; brigadier, gen. staff, Northern comd., India, 1930-34; dir., recruiting and organisation, W.O., 1934-37; comdr. 5th Div. from about May, 1937; lt.-gen., 1939; gov., Bermuda, 8th Oct., 1939.

BERNE, CAPT. JAMES LEO, O.B.E. (1918)—B. 1886; ed. Dulwich Coll.; 2nd Lieut., Royal Irish Regt., 1904; capt., 1910; served with Sierra Leone Batt. R.W.A.F.F., 1907-1912; served with Franco-Liberian bndry. comn., 1908 (read. thanks of French govt.); served with Anglo-French bndry. comn., 1911; ast. dist. comsnr., Somalil. and Prot., Sept., 1912; dist. comsnr., March, 1914; served with Admiralty war staff, intell. div., Apr. to Aug., 1916; accompanied mission to Abyssinia on the occasion of coronation of Empress Zauditu, 1917; 3rd cls. Star of Ethiopia, 1917; sen. ast. sec. to gov't. of Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1921; ag. ast. ch. sec., Sept., 1921 to May, 1923, Dec., 1923 to March, 1924; ag. prov. comsnr., Apr., 1930 to May, 1931 and Feb., 1932, Mar., 1934; dep. prov. comsnr., Feb., 1931; mem. leg. comn., 1931; prov. comsnr., Sept., 1934.

BERTEAU, F. C., I.S.O. (1914).—Ed. Victoria Coll., Jersey, 1865-72; ent. Newfoundland div. ser. as clk. H.M. Customs, 1878; collr. of cust., Labrador, 1881; clk. in col. sec.'s off., 1889; ch. clk., 1890; J.P. for col., 1893; mission to Ottawa to inquire into Canadian fin. system, with view of applying same to Newfdld., May, 1898; audr.-gen. Newfdld., July, 1898; ag. cashier, Newfoundland saving bank, 1911.

BERTRAM, SIR ANTON, KT. BACH. (1916), K.C. (1913).—Ed. at City of London sch., and Camb.; scholar of Caius Coll., 1887; Fellow, 1891; 1st cl. class. trip., part I, 1890; ditta. part II., 1891; Powis medal for Latin vers.; Chancellor's medal for classics, 1891; B.A., 1890; M.A., 1892; president, Union Soc., 1891; Tancred law studentship, Lincoln's Inn, 1890; called, 1893; atty.-gen., Bahamas, 1902; electd. to H. of Assem., June, 1903; ag. col. sec., May to Sept., 1903; admstd. gvt., Sept. to Oct., 1903; ag. ch. justice, Sep. Nov., 1906; chrmn. of comn. on the Out Is., 1906; puisne judge, Cyprus, 1906; atty.-gen., Caylon, 19th May, 1911; mem. of exec. and legis. couns.; ag. ch. justice, Apr., 1918; ch. justice, July, 1918; services lent to gvt. of Palestine, Dec., 1920 to May, 1921; ret., 1925; joint author, "Handbook to Workmen's Compensation Acts, 1897 and 1900."

BESSBOROUGH, 9TH EARL OF (great 1739), Rt. Hon. VERE BRAZON PONSONBY, P.C. (1911), G.C.M.G. (1931), C.M.G. (1919), B.A. (Cantab.), B. 1880; 2nd lieut., Bucks. I.Y., 1905-8; temp. capt., Suffolk yeo. and adjutant, 1918; served in Great War, 1914-18; L.O.O., 1907-10; M.P., Cheltenham, 1910 and Dover, 1913-20; J.P., Co. Kilkenny; gov.-gen. of the Dominion of Canada 1931-35.

BEST, CAPT. CHARLES CAIRN, M.C., L.S. M.N.Z.I.S.—B. 1894; ed. Auckland Gram. Sch. and Auckland Univ.; survey dept., N.Z., 1914-15; surv.-on-agr., Selangor, Aug., 1923; ast. supt., trig. surv., Sept., 1927; ast. supt., surv., June, 1928; ag. senr. do., Spore., Dec., 1934; ag. ch. survr., Malacca, Oct., 1938.

BEST, HON. SIR ROBERT WALLACE, K.C.M.G. (1908).—B. 1896; vice-pres. of the exec. comm. Australian Commonwealth; leader of the Deleg.
govt. in the Senate, Feb., 1907; min. for trade and customs, C. of A., 1908; now retd.

BEST, Sir Thomas Alexander Vans, K.C.M.G. (1932), K.B.E. (1926), C.M.G. (1916), C.B.E. (1918).—B. 1870; ed. Cheltenham Coll. and Magdalen Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1894; Taylorian Univ. scholar; gold medalist of French Ministry of pub. instruction; asst., B. Cent. Africa admn., 1896; judicial offr., Mar., 1898; ag. ch. judicial offr., Nov., 1899, to Mar., 1900; ag. vice-consul, Chinde, Aug., 1902, to Apr., 1903; ag. dep. consmr., Apr. to Dec., 1903, and June, 1905, to Jan., 1906; dist. rep., 1st cls., Apr., 1906; col. sec., Falkland Is., Oct., 1909; ag. gov., Dec., 1909, to Dec., 1910; attended Impl. Educn. Conf., 1911; col. sec., Leeward Is., Jan., 1913; ag. gov., May to Sept., 1914, Apr. to Aug., 1916, and from Jan., 1916, to Mar., 1919; reed. thanks of H.M.'s Govt. for services during disturbances in Antigua in Mar., 1918; col. sec., Trinidad, Aug., 1919; ag. gov., June-Aug., 1920, June, 1921 to Jan., 1922, June to Oct., 1923 and from Aug., 1924; lieut.-gov., Malta, 1925; O.A.G. for various periods in 1926, 1927, 1928 and 1929; gov., Windward Is., Sept., 1930; ret., 1933.

BETANCOURT, Nelson, F. Inst. Pet.—B. 1887; land surr.; 2nd asst. inspr. of mines, Trinidad, April, 1909; 1st ast. inspr., mines, Apr., 1921; ag. inspr., mines, in 1927, 1933 and 1934-36.

BETHEL, Charles Preval, L.S.O. (1929).—B. 1891; ag. 4th clk., post office, Bahamas, Apr. and Nov., 1909; cadet, Outislanda, Feb., 1910; 3rd clk., C.S.O., and clk. to pub. bd. of wks., New Providence, Sept., 1912; 2nd clk., C.S.O., Feb., 1914; ch. clk., C.S.O., Aug., 1919; enlisted for active serv., 1915, 2nd lieut., Mar., 1919; served in France; twice wounded; discharged from Army, Apr., 1919; resumed duties, May, 1919; ag. clk. in charge, col. sec.'s office, Aug. to Sept., 1923; ag. col. sec. and temp. mem., exec. coun., on various occasions, 1923-34; ag. A.D.C. to admstr., Sept. to Nov., 1925; asst. col. sec., July, 1928; ag. col., sec. and temp. mem., exec. coun., various periods, 1934-39.

BETTENCOURT-GOMES, Silvio Casimiro.—B. 1902; ed. at Stonyhurst Coll. and Edinburgh Univ.; M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.), M.R.C.P. (Edin.), D.T.M. & H. (Eng.); govt. med. offr., Br. Guiana, 1926; senr. phys., pub. hosp., Georgetown, Br. Guiana, 1938.

BETTINGTON, Digby Rowland Albemarle.—Ed. at United Serv. Coll., Westward Ho!; served with Natal Mounted Pol., 1898-1901; with 2nd Kitchener's Fighting Scouts, 1901-1902 (dangerously wounded, ment. in desps., Queen's med. and 5 clasps); inspr., mil. pol., Cyprus, 1903; inspr., pol., Sierra Leone, 1906; ag. consmr., pol. and sheriff on several occasions; dep.-comsmr. of pol. and dep.-supt., prisons, Gold Coast, 1910; base comdt., Togoland Field Force, 1914; "1914-15" Star, War and Victory meda.; title changed to dep. inspr-gen. of pol. and prisons, 1915; inspr.-gen. pol. and prisons, Gold Coast, 1917; inspr.-gen. pol., Gold Coast on separation of depts. of pol. and prisons, 1920; King's Police med., 1920; ret., 1924; commdt., pol., Bahamas, 1924; resigned, 1926; chief of pol. Bermuda, 1927.

BEVAN, Charles Edward, M.A., B.Ch. (Cantab.), M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P., D.T.M. & H.—B. 1905; ed. Bromsgrove schl., Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge and St. George's hosp., London; M.O., Nigeria, 1933; resigned in 1935 and joined Br. ambulance service in Ethiopia; reapptd. D.M.O., Cyprus, Oct., 1936; seconded as tuberculosis offr., Jan., 1938.

BEVERIDGE, Ian Alfred, B.Sc.—B. 1908; ed. George Watson's Coll. and Edinburgh Univ.; post grad. course, Imp. Forestry Inst., Oxford, 1929; asst. cons. of forests, Gold Coast, 1930.

BEVIR, Anthony, M.A.—B. 1895; scholar of Eton, 1909, and of Hertford Coll., Oxford, 1914; M.A., 1923; served with 7th Batt. King's Liverpool Regt., July, 1915 to Apr., 1919; twice ment. in desps.; asst. prin., C.O., 9th Feb., 1921; accompanied Mr. Ormsby-Gore on his visit to the West African Colonies, Jan.-May, 1926; pte-sec. to Mr. Ormsby-Gore, Feb., 1926; prin., 1st Apr., 1929; sec., C.O. confere., 1930; seconded to offices of Cabinet, Aug., 1939; ag. asst. sec., 3rd Nov., 1939.

BEVIS, James Henry.—B. 1904; ed. Univ. Coll. and Inst. of Educn., London, B.Sc., hons. botany, dipl. educn.; asst. mast., Queen's Coll., Br. Guiana, 1927.

BBWES, George Price Hope.—B. 1892; ed., Clifton Coll. and Royal Naval Coll., Osborne; asst. dist. consmr., Gold Coast, 25th Aug., 1920.

BEYERS, Brig.-Gen. Leonard.—B. 1894; perm. staff, Union defence forces, 1914-32; dir., prisons, Union of S. Africa, Sept., 1932.

BHARUCHA, Navroji Manekji, B.A., Cantab.—B. 1890; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Dec., 1913; addnl. pol. mag., Kurunegala, June, 1914; ag. pol. mag., Kurunegala, Apr., 1916; offic asst., Batticaloa kach., Jan., 1917; pol. mag., Nov., 1917; dist. judge, 1922; asst. attlm. offr., May, 1925; dist. judge, 1927; offr. cls., I, Oct., 1937.

BICKLE, W. H.—B. 1885; apptd. after compet. exam. clk. of the 2nd div., and assigned to C.O., 17th Mar., 1905; cler. offr. higher grade, 1st Apr., 1923; staff offr., 4th Sept., 1929.

BIDEN, Claude Eric De Beer.—B. 1887; ed. Radley Coll.; asst. audr., S. Nigeria, 1911; on active serv., attd. Nigerian Overseas Contgts., German E. Africa, and W. African Serv. Brig., 1917-19; senr. asst. audr., Nigeria, 1926; dep. audr., Gold Coast, 1930; mem., rly. retrenchment comtee., 1931; ag. audr., May, 1932; audr., Palestine and Trans-Jordan, May, 1933.

BIDMEAD, Kenneth Andrew.—B. 1909; pol. probnr., Hong Kong, Nov., 1929; asst. sup., pol., Aug., 1932; attd. Punjab pol., Jan.-Oct., 1935; asst. pol., Nov., 1939.

BIENEMAN, G. A. J., B.A.—B. 1889; ed. Dean Close, Cheltenham and Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; junr. supt., educn. dept., N. Nigeria, July, 1913; head of training coll., Oct., 1921; ch. inspr., educn., N. Provs., Nigeria, 1929; ag. asst. dir., educn., N. Provs., 1931, 1932, 1933 and 1934; ag. dir., educn., Nigeria, 1934 and 1936; asst. dir., educn., N. Provs., 1936; ag. dir., Apl.-Sept., 1938.

BIGELOW, Henry Veeder, K.C., B.A., LL.B., M.A.—B. 1874; ed. pub. schls., Truro, N.S., and Dalhousie Univ., B.A., 1894; LL.B., 1896; M.A., 1897; admitted to bar of N.S. 1896, practised law at Truro, N.S., and Regina, Sask.; K.C., Sask., 1913; judge, King's Bench, Sask., Feb., 1918.

BIGG, Wilfred Joseph.—B. 1897; boy clk., G.P.O., 22nd Nov., 1912; apptd. after compet. exam. clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv. and assigned to C.O., 1st Dec., 1914; on mil. ser. from 31st Aug., 1914, to 8th May, 1919; cler. offr., higher grade, 1922; asst. prin., 1st Aug., 1925; pte-sec. to perm. under sec., D.O. (Sir Ed. Harding), 3rd Feb., 1930; prin., 22nd June, 1931.
BILLING, ALFRED GEORGE, M.Q.I.S.—B. 1902; ed. Gram. Sch., Queensland, Australia; survey dept., Queensland, 1918-23; surv.-on-agr., F.M.S., Mar., 1924; asst. supt., Mar., 1928; title changed to senr. surv., Sept., 1938; ag. dep. ch. surv., S'pore., Sept., 1938.

BINGHAM, ROBERT PORTER.—B. 1903; ed. Dungannon Royal Schl. and Dublin Univ.; cadet, M.C.S., Jan., 1926; ag. 2nd asst. prot., Chin., S'pore, Oct., 1928; offr., ol. V., Jan., 1929; ag. D.O., X'mas Is., Dec., 1929; ag. 2nd asst. prot., Chin., S'pore, Apr., 1931; ag. asst. prot., Chin., Taiping, Nov., 1931; do., Malacca, Dec., 1932; offr., cl. IV., Jan., 1933; ag. prot. Chin., Kedah, Sept., 1933; ag. asst. prot., Chin., S'pore, Dec., 1935; offr., cl. III., Jan., 1938.

BINNIE, THOMAS REGINALD.—B. 1886; ed. Edin. Acad.; warehousekeeper, K. Lumpur, June 1921; supvr., cust., Oct., 1922; supt., cust., Oct., 1923; sr. supt., trade and cust., Jan., 1931; supvr., ext. duties, F.M.S. and asst. supt., rubber cont., S'pore in addn., Feb., 1938; dep. comnr., Selangor and Pahang, Nov., 1933; title changed to asst. comptlr., cust., Dec., 1938.

BIRCH, W. C.—Asst. analyst, E.A.P., July, 1914; senr. chemical offr., Apr., 1923.

BIRCH, WILLIAM SOMERSET, M.C., M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.).—B. 1889; ed. King's Coll. and King's Coll. Hosp.; served R.A.M.C. (S.R.), 1914-19; sen. asst. med. offr., Jamaica ment. hosp., 1923-24; med. supt., do., 1925-26; asst. med. supt., lunatic asylum, Barbados, 1927; med. supt., do., 1928; ag. oh. med. offr. for various periods, 1933-34.

BIRD, EDGAR CLARENCE FREDERIC.—B. 1886; ed. Xaverian Coll.; asst. ch., cust., Zanzibar Prot., Oct., 1914; ag. ch., cust., Jan. to Aug., 1915, May, 1916 to Feb., 1917, and Dec., 1917; marshal, H.B.M. Court for Zan zibar (in Prize), Jan. to Aug., 1915 and from Dec., 1917; immigr. offr., Sept., 1915; dep. compt., cust., Tanganyika Territory, Oct., 1920; ag. compt., cust., on various occasions, 1921-29; dep. compt., cust., Nigeria, 1930; compt., Nov., 1931.

BIRD, REGINALD.—B. 1893; ed. Merton Coll., Oxford; B.A. 1919; war serv., 1914-19; cadet, S.S., Oct., 1919; ag. dist. offr., Alor Gajah, June, 1920; asst. dist. judge, S'pore, Aug., 1922; asst. sec. to res., Selangor, July, 1924; dist. offr., K. Pilah, July, 1925; asst. advr., B. Pahat, Aug., 1928; offr., cls. III., Nov., 1929; ag. stamp and prob. offr., S'pore, Aug., 1933; ag. dep. treas., S.S., May, 1934; offr., cls. II., Nov., 1934; offr., cls. I., 1938.

BIRKINSHAW, FRANK.—B. 1887; asst. agrl. supt. and sc. mast., gram. schl., St. Vincent, Aug., 1912; agrl. instr., Mauritius, Jan., 1915; inspr., co-op. credit socs. in addn., Oct., 1915; agrl. supt., Sept., 1919; asst. agrl. inspr., Perak, F.M.S., June, 1920; agrl. field offr., Perak North, Dec., 1924; ditto P. Wellesley and Penang in addn., Apr., 1926; sr. agrl. field offr., Perak, Sept., 1931; state agrl. offr., Jan., 1934; ch. field offr., Aug., 1937.

BIRKITT, FRANK.—B. 1885; Imp. postal serv. (tels.) 1898-1902, mails, 1903-07; admtrv. (cler. and acctg.) 1908; staff record offr., 1909; postmtr., Nyasaland Prot. (various offices) 1912; (active serv., 1914-15, N.V.R., Nthn. Rhod. Forces), ag. asst. P.M.G. various occasions; 1st cl. olk., 1920; ob. act. and sktr., 1923; P.M.G., Br. Guiana, 1927; temp. M.L.C. in 1932-34; ob. act., Kenya, Uganda and Tanganyika Territory postal serv., 1935; senr. dep. P.M.G., 1936.

BIRSE, ARTHUR LOUIS.—B. 1893; cadet, S.S., Apr., 1921; collr., income tax, S'pore, Sept., 1921; treas., exec. cmte., Br. Malaya, Br. Emp. Exhibn., in addn., Jan., 1923; recvr., Alsagof Concession, Kubub, Mar., 1926; offr., cl. III., June, 1930; ; offr., cls. II., June, 1935; dist. offr., Larut and regtr., titles, Perak, Feb., 1936; dist. offr., Kinta, Sept., 1938.

BIRTWISTLE, WILLIAM.—B. 1890; ed. Queen Elizabeth's Grammar Schl., Blackburn; asst. naturalist (fisheries), min. of agr. and fisheries; directed research in dept. of oceanography, univ., Liverpool; fisheries economist, S.S. and F.M.S., Dec., 1924; offr.-in-ch., fisheries dept., S.S. and F.M.S., Apr., 1928; attended 5th Pacific Science Congress, Vancouver, B.C., S.S. and F.M.S. govt. deleg., June, 1933; dir. fisheries, S.S. and offr.-in-ch., fisheries dept., F.M.S., Jan., 1937.

BISCOE, VINCENT FREDERICK.—B. 1886; ed. at Cheltenham Coll. and Clare Coll., Camb.; B.A., June, 1908; 2nd lieut. London Rifle Brig. (Territorial Force), June, 1909; called to bar Inner Temple, Nov., 1910; asst. res., N. Nigeria, Aug., 1911; 2nd cls. dist. offr., Dec., 1919; ag. station mag., Dec., 1924.

BISHOP, CECIL WILLIAM EDWIN, B.Sc. (Eng.), A.M.Inst.C.E., M.Inst.W.E.—B. 1899; ed. Reigate Grammar Schl. and King's Coll., Lond. Univ.; war serv., 1918-19; engr., P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1922; ag. ex. engr., waterworks constr., 1935-36 and 1939.

BISSET, WILLIAM DAVID, O.B.E. (mil.), M.I.Mech.E.—B. 1889; ed. Gordon Schl., Huntly, Aberdeenshire, and Allen Glen's Schl., Glasgow; engnr. lieut., R.N., Jan., 1914; engnr. lieut. comdr., R.N., Apr., 1919; engnr.-in-ch., Misida dockyard, Malta, 1916-19; H.M.S. "Egmont," 1920; asst. engnr., marine dept., Nigeria, 1920; prin. engnr., 1933; ag. supt. engnr., for various periods, 1934-37.

BITHREY, WILLIAM BARREY.—B. 1888; ed. Peru's Schl., Alresford; B.S.A. pol., 1913; served with Rhodesia Column, S.W. Afr., 1914; seconded to Rhodesia Native Regt., 1916; supt., Nyasaland, pol., 1920; chmn., native language, exams. bd., comnr., pol., ch. inspr., prin., prin. immigrn. offr. and regtr., motor vehicles, 1938.

BLACK, ARCHIBALD MAULE.—Ed. S. African Coll., Cape Town; ent. div. serv., Cape Colony, 1895; addnl. asst. regtr., sup. ct., Cape Colony, 1903; asst. regtr., 1904; regtr. and taxing mast., sup. ct., Grahamstown, 1912; regtr. and taxing mast., sup. ct., Cape Town and high sheriff for prov. of Cape of Good Hope, 1928; on active service, 1914-19; ment. in desps.; awarded V.D., 1921; major, Union R. of O. (arty.).

BLACK, JOHN ALAN.—B. 1891; cadet, F.M.S., 1914; offr., cls. V., 1917; offr., cls. IV., 1921; offr., cls. III., Nov., 1926; asst. prot., Chinese, S'pore, Dec., 1926; ag. prot., Chinese, S'pore, Nov., 1929; do., Dec., 1930; offr., cls. II., Nov., 1931; ag. immigrn. offr., Jan., 1933; offr., cls. I.B., Jan., 1936; pres., munie. comm., Penang, July, 1937.

BLACK, JOHN GRAHAM.—B. 1896; cadet, B.S., May, 1920; pol. mag., asst. dist. judge and dep. regtr., sup. ct., Malacca, 1920; passed exam. June, 1921; coroner, Malacca, Mar., 1923; collr., law rev., May, 1923; offr., cls. V., May, 1923; prov. sec. to O.A.G., S.S., May, 1925; asst. dist. edir., Tapah, June, 1926; ditto, Kroh, Feb., 1927; offr., cls. IV., May, 1927; asst. advr., Trengganu, Nov.,

FURNES, Sir Robert Howard, Kt. Bach. (1929).—B. 1880; ed. King William’s Coll., Isle of Man; solr. (hons.), 1902; practised at bar of B. Honduras, 1906-13; regar-gen., B. Honduras, 1913; served with B. W. I. Regt., 1915-19; called to bar, Lincoln’s Inn, 1919; mag., Tanganyika Territory, Jan., 1920; senr. mag., Apr., 1921; solr. gen., Trinidad, Nov., 1923; ch. just., Barbados, Oct., 1926; do., Jamaica, 1936.

FURNES-SMITH, Cecil, Barrister-at-Law.—B. 1890; ed. Birkenhead Schl. and St. John’s Coll., Camb.; B.A., 1912; LL.B., 1913; asst. dist. comsrr., G. Coast, Apr., 1914; dist. comsrr., 1921; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1922; crown coun., Mar., 1925; ag. solr.-gen., May-Oct., 1927; ag. circuit judge, 1929; solr.-gen., Tanganyika Territory, Aug., 1932; ag. atty.-gen. in 1933; atty.-gen., Zanzibar, Mar., 1936.

FURSE, Major R. D., C.M.G. (1935), D.S.O.—B. 1887; ed. Eton and Balliol Coll., Oxford, B.A.; asst. priv. sec. to sec. of state (Mr. Lewis now Lord) Harcourt), Dec., 1910 to Aug., 1914; on active service in 1st King Edward’s Horse, K.O. D.R., 5th Aug., 1914 to 26th Nov., 1918; served in France and Italy, Apr., 1915 to 26th Nov., 1918; promoted capt., 1914; major, 1916; wounded, 1917; D.S.O., July, 1918; Bar to D.S.O., gazetted, Mar., 1919; twice ment. in despatches, asst. priv. sec. (appointments) to sec. of state (Lord Milner), May, 1919; Mr. Winston Churchill, Feb., 1921; Duke of Devonshire, Oct., 1922; priv. sec., (appointments) to sec. of state, Mr. Thomas, Jan., 1924; Mr. L. C. M. S. Amery, Nov., 1924; Lord Passfield, 8th June, 1929; visited on C.O. business—Canada, 1922, 1923, 1928; Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, Java, Malaya, Ceylon, 1928-29; South, Central and East Africa and the Sudan, 1935-36; mem. of Emp. Forestry Conferences in Canada, 1923; Australia and New Zealand, 1928; South Africa, 1935; mem. of comittee for Forestry of Oxford Univ.; asst. sec., C.O., Oct., 1930.

GAHAN, Edward John Beresford, B.A., B.A.I., A.M.I.C.E.—War serv., R.A.S.C. 1914-19; coal comm., 1919-21; engnr. asst., M.G.W.R. (I), 1923; asst. engr., K.U.R. & H., 1924; sr. asst. engr., 1928; dist. engr., 1931; senr. engr., Nigeria rly., 1938; ag. ch. engr., Jan.-June, 1939.

GALSWORTHY, Arthur Norman.—B. 1916; ed. Emanuel Schl. and Corpus Christi Coll., Camb.; senr. schol. of Corpus Christi Coll., 1936-37; let. cls. mod. languages tripods, pt. I, 1936 and pt. II, 1937; apptd. after compet. exam., asst. prin., C.O., 5th Oct., 1938.

GALWAY, 8th Viscount (or. 1727) George Vere Abundell Monkton-Arundell, P.C. (1937), G.C.M.G. (1935), D.S.O. (1917), O.B.E. (1919).—B. 1882; ed. Eton and Christ Church, Oxford; Sherwood Rangers Yeomanry, 1900-04; 1st Life Guards, 1904; adjt., 1908; capt., 1911; staff capt., 4th Cavalry Brig., 1914; D.A.A. and Q.M.G., 2nd Cavalry Divn., 1915; A.A. and Q.M.G., 1917; brevet lieut.-col., 1919; commd. Life Guards, 1925-29; col. commd., Hon. Arty. Cov., 1933; gov.-gen. and comdr.-in-ch., New Zealand, 1935.

GALWAY, Lt.-Col. The Right Hon. Sir Henry Lionel, K.C.M.G. (1910), C.M.G. (1899), D.S.O. (1896).—B. 1859; ed. Cheltenham Coll. and Sandhurst; entered army, May, 1878; promoted lieut., Mar., 1881; capt., Oct., 1887; brevet-maj., May, 1897; maj., Mar., 1899; and lt.-col., Apr., 1901; apptd. dep. commr. and vice-consul, Oil Rivers prot., Mar., 1891; dep. commr. and consul, Niger Coast prot., Jan., 1897; and divn. commr. Niger Coast prot. (now South. Nigeria), Apr., 1899; ag. consul-gen. Niger Coast prot., Aug. to Nov., 1896; Jan., 1897; Feb., 1898, to Jan., 1899; ag. high commr., South. Nigeria, Mar. to Dec., 1900; Brass expdn., 1895 (desp., medal with clasp, D.S.O.); Benin expdn., 1897 (desp., clasp, brevet majority); Aro expdn., as chief political officer, 1901-02 (desp., medal with clasp); gov., St. Helena, 1902; gov., Gambia, 30th Sept., 1911; gov., S. Australia, 27th Feb., 1914; assumed govt., 18th Apr., 1914, retired, 1920.

GALWAY, John Patrick Francis.—Ed. St. Francis Xavier’s Coll., Liverpool; clk., vety. pathological lab., Kabete, Aug., 1910; seconded, mily. serv., 1915; corp., E. African Vty. Corps, 1st June, 1916; lieut. ditto, 17th Oct., 1917; lieut., 3rd K.A.R.; “1914-15” Star, Gen. Serv. and Victory med.; labour inspn. offr., E. Africa Prot., Apl., 1919; office supt., P.W.D., Dec., 1922.

GAMBLE, Frederick Charles.—B. 1891; ed. Felsted and Wadham Coll., Oxford, B.A. (hons. jurisprudence) 1914; asst. dist. commr., E.A.P., Feb., 1915; transp. offr., N. Frontier dist., 1916; ag. dist. commr., 1918; res. mag., July, 1923; offr. attlr., Mombassa town planning scheme, 1929; judge, high ct., Uganda and mem., ct. of appl. for Eastern Africa, 1935.

GAMBLES, Robert Moylan, B.A. (Cantab.), M.R.C.V.S.—B. 1910; ed. Westminster Schl. (King’s schl.) and Trinity Coll., Cambridge (cl. II nat. sci. tripods, pt. I in 1931); R. (Dick) Vety. Coll., Elin. (C.O. scholarship) and Univ. of Edin.; vety. offr., Cyprus, Jan., 1936; ag. ch. vety. offr., June-Oct., 1935 and Apr.-Aug., 1937; vety. resch. offr., Palestine, 1938.

GAME, Air Vice-Marshal Sir Philip Woolcott, G.C.V.O. (1937), G.B.E. (1929), K.C.B. (1924), K.C.M.G. (1935), C.B. (1919), D.S.O. (1915).—B. 1876; ed. Charterhouse; ent. R.A., 1893; capt., 1901; adjt., 1902; major, 1912; air vice-marshal, 1922; G.S.O., 3rd and 2nd
grade, W.O., 1910-14; served, S. Africa, 1901-02 (deeps., Queen's Med. five claps); European war, 1914-18 (deeps. six times); dir., training and organization, Air Ministry, 1919-22; commanded R.A.F., India, 1922-23; air. mem. for personnel on air cun., 1923-28; ret. list, 1929; gov., New South Wales, 1930-35.

GANADO, Prof. Edgar, LL.D.—B. 1884; matric., Malta Univ., 1901; LL.D., 1910; prof. of law, 1921; ag. pub. pros. and treas. coun., 1928; judge, 1929; ex. in law, 1930.

GANADO, Roberto F., LL.D.—B. 1875; ed. Malta Lyceum; matric., Malta Univ., 1891; LL.D., Malta, 1898; bar, Malta, 1899; advoc. for poor, 1905; mag., judl. pol., 1918; examr. laws, Malta Univ., 1919; chmn., licensing bd., 1920; visitor, notarial acts Nov., 1921; ag. crown advoc., June, 1922; ag. pub. pros. and treas. coun., July to Oct., 1922; chmn., bd. of prison visitors, 1924; ag. judge, supr. cts., June to Sept., 1924; mem., gen. coun. of Univ. of Malta, 1924; judge, supr. cts., Sept., 1925.

GANDY, Gerard Horace, Lt.-Cmdr., R.N. (retd.).—B. 1896; land survr., P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1927; re-apptd., harbr. survr., P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1931; land survr., 1934; attched. tech. sec.'s off., Apr., 1939; re-called Royal Navy, Sept., 1939.

GANE, Percival Carleton, M.A. (Oxon.), LL.B. (Cape).—B. 1874; ed. Kingswood Schl., Bath and Jesus Coll., Oxford; admitted advoc., S. Africa, 1903; K.C., 1919; ag. judge many occasions, 1920-34; puisne judge, eastern dists. local divn., sup. ct., S. Africa, 1934.

GARDINER, Edmund Austin, B.Sc., A.K.C., A.M.I.C.E., A.M.I.M.E., A.M.I.S.E., Chd. Civ. and Mech. Eng., King's Coll., Lond. Univ.—B. 1898; war survr., 1916-19; asst. engrnr., P.W.D., Malaya, Apr., 1924; ex. engrnr., Apr., 1933; ag. sr. engrnr., Dec., 1937.

GARDINER, Hon. James Garfield, B.A., LL.D., (Assiniboia, S.).—B. 1883; ed. pub. schls.; el., Sask. legislature at by-elec., 1914; re-elec., 1917, and at g.e., 1921 by acclm.; min., highways and min. in ch., bureau of lab. and industries, 1922; re-elec. without contest after assuming office at by-elec., 1922; re-elec. g.e., 1925; premier, Sask., 1926; prov. treas., 1926-27; min. of educn., 1928-29; re-elec., g.e., 1929; resigned as premier, 1929; re-elec., g.e., 1934; premier and prov. treas., Sask., 1934; resigned as premier when applt. min., agr. in Rt. Hon. W. L. Mackenzie King's cabinet, 1935; first elec., H. of C., Canada at a by-elec., Jan., 1936.

GARDNER, Harold Mence, O.P.E. (1938).—B. 1889; ed. Worcester and Merton Coll., Oxford, B.A. (hons.) dipl., forestry; asst. conservator of forests, E.A.P., Mav., 1914; senr. asst. conservator, forests, Kenya, Dec., 1923; ag. conservator, 1925 and 1927; conservator, 1928; nom. M.L.C.

GARDNER, John Hyslop, O.B.E. (1939), B.Sc.—B. 1883; ed. Kelvinside Acad. and Univ., Glasgow; asst. engrnr., Basutoland, 1909; govt. engrnr., Swariland, 1919; served with R.E. Flanders, 1916-18; D.P.W., 1938.

GARLAND, Neill, A.R.T.C., B.Sc., A.M.I.N.A.—B. 1899; ed. Alloa Acad., R. Tech. Coll., and Glasgow Univ.; flying offr., R.F.C. & R.A.F., France, 1917-19; asst. govt. marine survr., Hong Kong, 1928.

GARVEY, Francis Willcocks.—B. 1882; served in S. Africa, first in the ranks and afterwards as transport offr.; served Transvaal town pol., 1904-08; asst. commr., pol., S. GARVEY, Ronald Herbert, M.A. (Cantab.), F.R.A.I.—B. 1903; ed. GATER, BOSSLEY ALAN REX, M.A., Dip. Agric. (Cantab.), D.I.C., F.R.M.S., F.E.S., F.Z.S.—B. 1896; war serv., 1914-19; asst. entomologist dept. of agric., F.M.S., Nov., 1922; malaria resch. offr., Nov., 1926; entomologist Inst. Med. Resch., 1927; prof., biology, King Edward VII Coll. of Medicine, S'pore, Aug., 1930; del. to 8th cong. of Far Eastern Assoc. of Trop. Med., Dec., 1930.

GATES, CHARLES EDWARD, M.A. (Cantab.).—B. 1889; ed. Uppingham Schol. and Sydney Sussex Coll., Cambr.; European mast., S.S. and F.M.S., Feb., 1924; headmast., High Schol., Kajang, June, 1929; ag. headmast., Vict. Inst., June, 1937.

GAULD, HENRY WILLIAM.—B. 1886; G.N. of Scotland Rly., 1900-13; R.E., 1915-19; traffic inspr., K.U.R. and H., 1919; dist. traffic supt., cls. II., 1928; do., cls. I., 1936.

GAUNT, A. E.—B. 1897; entd. C.O., Aug., 1913; apptd. asst. clk., Oct., 1915; on mil. ser. from Dec., 1915 to Mar., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; cler. offr., higher grade, 28th Dec., 1928.

GEAR, HARRY SUTHERLAND.—B. 1903; B.Sc. (1st cls. hona.) 1926; M.B., B.Ch. Witwatersrand Univ., S. Afr., 1928; D.P.H., Univ. London, 1931; D.T.M. & H., R.C.P.S. Eng., 1932; med. offr., N. Inst., Mauritius, July, 1923; asst., entomologist, sp., malaria serv., Feb., 1927; asst. entomologist, hookworm and malaria bch., July, 1932; entomologist, med. and health dept., 1934; author of various papers on economic and medical entomology.

GEDDES, WILLIAM BUTLER.—B. 1880; under sec. of just., N.S.W., Jan., 1933; pub. trustee, Jan., 1936.

GEORGE, NANCY MARGARET FANNY.—B. 1900; ed. St. Catherine's High Schol., Malta, Devonport Secondary Schol., Froebel Training Coll., Bedford; mistress, Achimota Coll., Gold Coast, Jan., 1928.

GEORGI, MAJOR CHARLES DENIS VICTOR, O.B.E. (Mil.), B.Sc. (Lond.), F.I.C., Dulwich Coll.); Univ. of Lond., Univ. Coll.—B. 1890; ast. agrl. chem., F.M.S., Nov., 1920; senr. chem., agrl. dept., S.S. and F.M.S., Nov., 1936.

HOLLIS, SIR ALFRED CLAUD, G.C.M.G. (1934), K.C.M.G. (1927), C.M.G. (1911), C.B.E. HOLLOWAY, JOHN EDWARD.—B. 1890; B.A. (hons. hist.), 1910, Univ. C. of G.H. (Victoria Coll.); res. mast., Grey Coll. Schl., Bloemfontein, 1911-13; mem., coun. of examrs., O.F.S., 1912-13; D.Sc. SANDYS, MELVILL KEVERNE TRELAWNY, M.A. (Oxon.).—B. 1890; on mily. serv., Aug., 1914; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Nov., 1919; attd., Ratnapura kach., Nov., 1919; office asst. to govt. agt., N.W. Prov., Mar., 1922; dist. judge, Anuradhapura, July, 1925; pol. mag., Kurunegala, Oct., 1926; ag. agt., Hambantota, May, 1927; ag. dist. judge, Tangalla, June, 1927; nat. govt. agt., Uva, July, 1927; asst. settlmt. officer, Jan., 1929; asst. govt. agt., Kalutara, Oct., 1931; do., Mannar, Nov., 1931; do., Trincomalee, Mar., 1933; do., Matale, Nov., 1933; dist. judge, Badulla, Oct., 1936; ag. govt. agt., N.P., May, 1937; chmn., mun. coun., Kandy, and addnl. asst. govt. agt., Nov., 1937.

SANKERALLI, ESAU JYMSHEL, M.D., Ch.B., B.A.O. (Queen's University, Belfast). D.T.M. (Liverpool), L.M. (Dublin), D.P.H. (Felfast).—B. 1898; govt. med. offr., Trinidad, 1925; asst. res. surg., col. hosp., 1929; junr. med. inspr., health, Aug. 1935; S.M.O.H., Jan., 1936.

SARAVANAMUTTY, PAIKIASOTHI.—B. 1894; B.A., Lond.; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Aug., 1919; attd., Colombo, kach., Aug., 1919; attd. to Matale Kach., June, 1920; addnl. dist. judge, Radulla, Mar., 1921; pol. mag., Dandagamuwa, Sept., 1921; ditto, Kurunegala, June, 1922; addnl. asst. govt. agt., Colombo, Mar., 1923; addnl. asst. dir., educn., Dec., 1925; asst. govt. agt., Mullaitivu, Dec., 1926; dist. judge, Kegalle, Mar., 1929; dist. judge, Kalutara, Apr., 1932; asst. govt. agt., Kalutara, Apr., 1933; rubber contr., May, 1934; tea contr. in addn., Apr., 1935.

SARGENT, CAPT. R. G., M.B.E. (1928), A.I.N.A., F.R.G.S.—Port offr., Kenya, Jan., 1917; port capt., K.U.R. & H., 1925.

SAUNDERS, MAJOR ALAN, O.B.E. (1932), M.C. (1917).—B. 1886; ed. Christ's Hosp.; Indian pol., 1906-14; Great War, 1914-20; France, Flanders, Palestine; wounded twice; three times sent in despa.; dep. inspr. genl., Palestine pol., 1926; King's pol. med., Sept., 1929; commr., Nigeria pol., 1936; inspr.-gen., pol. and prisons, Palestine, Nov., 1937.

SAUNDERS, GODFREY ESTRIDGE.—B. 1884; offr. of cust., Cape Town, 1901; 1st grade examir., Mossel Bay, 1915; prin. clk., Pretoria, 1928; senr. inspr., Johannesburg, 1931; survr., cust., Port Elizabeth, 1933; investigation offr., London, 1933; ch. inspr., Pretoria, 1936; asst. dep. commr., Pretoria, 1937; dep. commr., 1938.

SAUNDERS, PHILIP HENRY NORMAN.—B. 1890; ed. Queen's Coll., Br. Guiana; successively 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd cls. clk., P.W.D., Br. Guiana, 1911-24; sec., bd. of examnrs. for land surveyors, 1917; sec., bd. of industrial training, 1930; acctg. clk., P.W.D., 1931; sec., advisory comte of sea defences, 1932; sec., sea defence bd., 1933; sec., prisoners' aid comte, 1935.

SAUNDERS-JONES, DAVID WILLoughby.—B. 1899; ed. Christ Coll., Brecon; Indian Army, 1917-23; on service in Waziristan, Egypt and Palestine; wounded in Palestine, 1919; asst. dist. commr., Zanzibar, Feb., 1924; ag. pte. sec., Br. res. in 1925 and from Aug., 1930-Mav., 1931; ag. prov. commr., Pemba, June, 1930 and July, 1932-Feb., 1933; asst. sec. and pte. sec. to Sultan, 1935-38; admin. offr., Nyasaland, 1939.

SAUVE, HON. ARTHUR, P.C. (Can.).—B. 1875; ed. Seminary of Ste. Therese and l'Univ. de Montreal; 1st el. to legis. assem., Quebec, g.e., 1908; re-elec., g.e., 1912, 1916, 1919, 1923 and 1927; el. to H. of C., Canada, g.e., 1930; P.M.G., in Bennett Cabinet, 1930; re-elec. by accl. after assuming office, Aug., 1930.; mem., senate, 1935.

SAVAGE, ALFRED WILLIAM LUNGLAY.—B. 1903; Crown Agents office, 1920; seconded to treasv., N. Rhodesia, 1921; asst. treas., 1928; mun. coun. audr., 1930 and 1931; sec., taxn.comm., 1934; dep. treas., Fiji, 1935; sec., pub. serv. reorganisation comte., 1936; acct-gen. and dep. treas., 1937; ag. financial sec. and col. treas., and ex-officio M.L.C., 1937; chmn., agric. bank comte., 1938; offi. M.L.C., 1938; ag. financial sec., and col. treas., July-Sept., 1938.

*SAVAGE, Rt. HON. MICHAEL JOSEPH, P.C. (1936).—B. 1872; mem., N.Z. H. of R. since 1919; leader of labour party, 1933; prime min., min. of external affrs. and native min., 1935; rep. N.Z. at coronation, 1937; leader, N.Z. deleg. to Imp. Confce., 1937.

SAVARY, JOHN LEWIS HENRY WILLIAM.—B. 1884; col. schol., Trinidad, 1901; Gray's Inn, 1902; prizeman in evidence, procedure and criminal law exam., 1904; barrister-at-law, Nov., 1905; practised at bar, Trinidad, 1906-24; retainer from Trinidad govt. as junr. coun. to atty.-gen., Jan., 1916-Dec., 1923; ag. solr.-gen., in 1921, 1922 and 1923; registr. and marshal and regist.-gen. and prim. registr., West Indian ct. of appeal, Jan., 1925; ag. puisne judge in 1925 and 1926; puisne judge, Br. Guiana, 1928; ag. ch. just. in 1932, 1934 and 1936; puisne judge, Gold Coast, June, 1937; judge, high ct., Jamaica, 1939.
SAWARD, Capt. Sidney Carmon, M.C. (1916), M.M. (1916).—B. 1889; fellow of surveyors' inst.; served with 509 (1-1) Lond. Field Coy., R.E., 6th divn.; home serv., Aug. to Dec., 1914; France and Germany, Dec., 1914 to June, 1919; Ireland, June to Aug., 1919; commdg., cadre, 12th Field Co., R.E.; comsmd., Sept., 1915; lieut., June, 1916; capt., Oct., 1918; ag. major, Dec., 1918 to Jan., 1919; ment. in despa., Mar., 1919; survr., Gold Coast, Nov., 1919; field supervisor Apr., 1924; ag. dep. survr.-gen. on various occasions, 1925-32; ag. survr.-gen., Feb.-June, 1927; asst. survr.-gen., Apr., 1929; ag. survr.-gen., Mar.-Aug., 1934, and Mar.-Aug., 1936; dir. of surveys, 1938.

SAXTON, Sidney Waring.—Ed. Toulouse (France), and Dean Close Schl., Cheltenham; paymr. cadet, R.N., July, 1905; paymr.-lieut. comdr., Mar., 1918; 1st cls. French interpreter, lent to C.O. and apptd. asst. dist. comsnr., G. Coast, Sept., 1914, but did not take up apptmt., having resumed duty in H.M. Navy for the period of the war; assumed duties as junr. asst. col. sec., G. Coast, Apr., 1919; ag. asst. col. sec., May, 1919; ag. dist. comsnr., Accra, and ag. trav. comsnr. for Accra-Akwapim and Birrim dists., Oct., 1919; invalided, H.M. Navy, 1920; passed Tropical African service course (all subjects, 2nd part); barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1925; promoted pay comdr., ret. list, 1927; d.c.p. prov. comsnr., 1930; prov. comsnr., 1938.

SAYERS, Eldred Frank.—B. 1889; ed. King's Coll. Schl., Wimbledon, St. John's Coll., Cambridge, and Grenoble Univ., B.A., LL.B. (Cantab.); barrister-at-law (Inner Temple), Apr., 1913; passed lower and higher stand. exams. in Temne, and lower stand. exam. in Koranko; war service, E. Africa, 1918; asst. dist. comsnr., Sierra Leone, Jan., 1915; dist. comsnr., Aug., 1922.

SAYERS, Gerald Fleming.—B. 1893; ed. Westminster and Christ Church, Oxford; B.A. (hons.) 1914; asst. dist. comsnr., E. Africa Prot., Feb., 1915; ag. senr. asst. sec., Nov., 1919 to July, 1920; asst. sec., Tanganyika territory, July, 1920; ag. senr. asst. sec., for various periods 1920-24; clk. to exec. coun., Sept., 1923; attd. to C.O., Aug., 1924 to Sept., 1925 and from July to Sept., 1930; clk., leg. coun., 1926-32; ag. asst. ch. sec., on various occasions, 1927-1931; asst. ch. sec., 1932; asst. ch. sec., Nyaaland Prot., 1933; ag. ch. sec., Feb., 1934; dep. ch. sec., Tanganyika Territory, May, 1935; mem., exec. and leg. couns.; ag. ch. sec., in 1935 and 1937; adminstr. sec., 1937; edtr., Handbook of Tanganyika Territory, 1930.

SCAMMELL, Ernest Henry.—B. 1873; ed. privately; sec. various business concerns, 1891-1907; visited Australia, engaged in business and journalism in Canada, 1907-1913; organizing sec., Canadian Peace Centenary Association, under the auspices of the govt. of Canada, 1913; asst. cable censor, dept. of militia and defence, Canada, 1915; sec., mil. hosps. comsnr., Canada, 1915; asst. dep. min. and sec., dept. of soldiers' civil re-establishment, Canada, 1918; negotiated reciprocal agreements between Canadian, British and United States Govts., regarding treatment and training of Naval and Military Forces resident in these countries, 1919; sec., pensions divn., dept. of pensions and national health, 1931; Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Secretaries (London); Fellow of the Royal Colonial Institute (London); mem. of the Exec. of the Canadian Peace Centenary Assoc.

SCHARFF, John William, B.A., M.D., B.A.O., B.Ch., D.P.H. (T.C.D.), D.T.M. & H. (Lond.).—B. 1895; surgm. sub.-lieut., R.N.V.R., July, 1915; health offr., S.S., Nov., 1920; lect. in biology, King Edward VII Coll. of Medicine in addn., May, 1921; hon. sec. for Malaya of the Far Eastn. Assoc. of Trop. Med., Aug., 1921; health offr., Malacca, June, 1929; sr. health offr., Penang, May, 1928; offr. deleg. to 8th cong. of Far Eastn. Assoc. of Trop. Med., Bangkok, Dec., 1930; superscale offr., grade A, Jan., 1935; ch. health offr., Spore, July, 1935.

SCHEMBRI, Judge Salvatore, LL.D.—B. 1881; matric., Malta Univ., 1899; LL.D., 1907; ag. judge, Malta, 1936; judge, 1937.

SCHMIDT, Carl Friedrich, B.A.—Civ. serv. law clk., law dept., Cape, May, 1893; control and audit office, July, 1893; asst. examnr. of accts., Jan., 1894; examnr., May, 1898; ch. examnr., July, 1907; inspr. of accts., Jan., 1909; prin. clk., Apr., 1912; sec., educ. dept., Bloemfontein, 16th Aug., 1915; ag. dir. of educn., O.F.S., July, 1918; dir. of educn., O.F.S., June, 1920; sec. for interior, Sept., 1926; contr. and audr.-gen., 1929; rector, Pretoria univ., 1935.

SCHMITT, Louis John, A.I.C.A., F.C.A.A.—B. 1885; ed. Victoria Parade coll., Australia; acct., for some years; sec., N.Z. bd. of trade prior investig. tribunal, 1919; investig. acct., bd. of trade, 1921; sec. to advisey. coun., N.Z. sect., Wembley exhibn., 1924; dep. gov't. comsnr., Dunedin internat. exhibn., 1925; advy. acct., industries and commerce dept., 1927; mem. (rep. employers), N.Z. ct. of arbitn., 1928; N.Z. govt. tourist and trade comsnr. in Australia, 1930-35; sec. and gen.-man. N.Z. dept. of industries and commerce, tourist and publicity, 1935.

SCHNEIDER, George Albert Wilhelm.—B. 1884; ed. Pretoria High Schl. and S.African Coll., Cape Town; solr., sup. ct., Transvaal; civ. serv., Transvaal, 1907; ch. clk., dept. of lands, 1931; under-sec. for agr., 1935.

SCHOCHE, August Arnold.—B. 1883; ed. Berne, Switzerland; graduated, Leiden, LL.D. and called to bar, Middle Temple, 1910; ent. Union pub. serv., 1911; priv. sec. to min. of justice, 1913-16; professional asst. to attr.-gen. (Transvaal), 1916-24; solr.-gen., Cape Eastern Dist., Aug., 1924; law adviser and Dutch draughtsman, dept. of just., Pretoria, Sept., 1925; senr. law adviser, Oct., 1931.

SCHOKMAN, Clive Conrade.—B. 1897; 4th sqn., prisons, Ceylon, Jan., 1924; 1st do., Apr., 1928; inspr.-gen., prisons, Mar., 1932.

SCHOLEFIELD, Guy Hardy, D.Sc. (Lond.), O.B.E. (1919).—Ed. Tokomairiro High Schl. and Univ. of N.Z. (Bowen and Macmillan Brown prizeman) and Univ. of London; ch. librarian, gen. assembly liby. and contrlr., dominion archives, N.Z., 1926.

SCHOLEFIELD, William.—Dep. clk., res. mag.s., etc., Jamaica, Mar., 1913; clk., res. mag.s., etc., Feb., 1917; asst. comsnr. and mag., Turks and Caicos Islands, July, 1919; ag. comsnr., ditto, Sept. to Oct., 1920; ag. res. mag., Jamaica, on various occasions, 1922-26.

SCHOLES, Alwyn Denton, M.A. (Hons. Cantab.).—B. 1910; ed. Cheltenham Coll. and Selwyn Coll., Cambridge; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1934; practised at English bar, Central Crim. Ct., Midland circuit and Birmingham, Lincoln, Leicester, Northampton, Warwick, Nottingham, Bedford and Derby City and County sessions; dist. mag., Gold Coast, Apr., 1938.
SCHREINER, OLIVER DENEYS.—B. 1890; ed. Rondebosch H. Schl., S.A. Coll. Schl., S.A. Coll. (Cape Town), Trin. Coll., Camb. (fellow 1916); barrister, Inner Temple; M.C., 1916; advoc., Johannesburg, 1920-37; K.C., 1935; judge, supr. ct., S.A., T.P.D., 1937.

SCHUMANN, THOROD E. WERNER, B.A., M.Sc., Ph.D.—B. 1896; ed. Stellenbosch, S.A.; Gottingen, Germany and Yale, U.S.A.; lect. in physics and maths., Rhodes Univ. Coll., Grahamstown, 1918-19; and at Stellenbosch, 1920-21; dir., fuel research inst. of S. Africa, June, 1931, resgd., Feb., 1933; ch. meteorologist, Union of S.A., Sept., 1933.

SCICLUNA, HANNIBAL P., M.B.E. (1935), Hon. M.A. (Oxon.) (1938). L.P.—B. 1880; ed. St. Ignatius' Coll., Malta; matric., Malta Univ., 1897; ent. Malta civ. serv., 1902; legal procurator, 1905; sec. and regiar., Malta Univ., 1913-20; rep. of gov't. emigr. dept. in devastated regions, France, 1920; attd., ministry of justice, 1921; esquire, Order of St. John of Jerusalem (Rome), 1910; Officier d'Academie (France), 1921; mem. of the Societe Academique d'Histoire Internationale de Paris, 1923; librn., Malta public library, July, 1923; ag. dir. of museum, 1938.

SCOTLAND, ERICA ELEANOR.—Ent. C.O. as typist, July, 1913; shorthand writer, Aug., 1918; cler. offr., 9th Mar., 1922.

SCOTT, MAJOR CHARLES ALEXANDER.—B. 1893; ed. Edinburgh Univ.; M.A. (Edinburgh); European mast., S.S., Apr., 1923; headmast., Rangoon Rd., schl., S'pore, Aug., 1932; inspr., schls., N. Semban, June, 1934; headmast., King George V schl., Seremban, Feb., 1935; ag. headmast., English Coll., J. Bahru, Oct., 1936; ag. supt., educn., Johore, Apr., 1937.

SCOTT, HENRY HAROLD, M.D., London Univ.; F.R.C.P., London; F.R.S., Edin.; D.P.H.; M.R.C.S., Eng.; D.T.M. & H. (Camb.); Fell. of Royal Soc. of medicine; Fell. of Royal Inst. of preventive medicine; Fell. of Soc. of tropical medicine and hygiene.—Ed. at St. Bart's and St. Thomas's hosps.; Univ. Colls., London and Copenhagen; prosecutor, 1894; asst. demonstrator in Materia Medica, 1895; asst. house physician, 1897; house physician, 1898, all at St. Thomas's hosp.; res. med. offr., Teignmouth hosp., 1898; serv. in S. African War (Queen's medal with 5 clasps); med. offr. in charge bacteriological and X-Ray depts., mil. hosp., Maritzburg, 1903; M.O. in charge Fort Napier hosp. for women and children, 1904; res. med. offr., Kingsbury and Neasden isolation hosp., 1910; bacteriologist to Willeiden Dist. Coun., 1910; govt. bacteriologist and fermentation chemist, Jamaica, 1910; is also pathologist to Kingston gen. hosp.; mem. of med. coun., board of examiners, quarantine board, and cent. board of health, Jamaica; during 1915-1917, seconded for war service; bacteriologist at Command Laboratory, Aldershot, 1915; in charge No. XIII, mobile laboratory, 1916; pathologist and med. specialist, Cambridge hosp., Aldershot, 1916; govt. pathologist dir., serum inst. Hong Kong, 1919; lect. on path. and med. jurisprudence, Hong Kong Univ., 1919; Milner research fellowship, L.S.H. and T.M., 1925; lect. trop. disease, Westminster hosp., med. schl., 1926; examnr., D.M.T. and H. Eng., 1927; med. sec., col. med. research countee, 1928.

SCOTT, Sir JOHN, K.B.E. (1932), C.M.G. (1923).—B. 1878; ed. Bath Coll. and King's Coll., Cambridge (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1901; prin. asst. col. sec., Apr., 1917; dep. ch. sec. to govt., Nigeria, Feb., 1921; ch. sec., Tanganyika Territory, Jan., 1924; admstd. govt. for various periods, 1924-29; col. sec., S.S., 1929; admstd. govt., various occasions, 1929-31; ret., Aug., 1933.

SCOTT, MARGARET.—Ed. Sherbourne Schl. for Girls; V.A.D. nurse, Brit. R. Cross, 1915-19; housekeeper's dipl., Edin. Sch. of Domestic Econ., 1920; matron, Achimota, 1925.

SCOTT, R. R., C.M.G. (1939), M.C., M.B., B.S. (Durham), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.P.H. (Lond.).—R.A.M.C. (S.R.), Aug., 1914; ment. in desps., 1919; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Mar., 1919; senr. med. offr. of health, Apr., 1924; dep. dir., sanv. serv., 1932; D.M.S., 1935.

SCOTT, WALTER RICHARDSON.—B. 1899; ed. Durham, 1922; pol. probationer, Hong Kong, 1922; passed final exam. in Chinese, 1924; asst. supt. pol., 1924; J.P., 1925; attd. Indian pol. and passed in Urdu, 1926; passed Punjabi, 1928; pvt. sec. to O.A.G., in addn., 1928; ditto to gov. in addn., Jan. to Mar., 1929; hon. A.D.C., to gov., 1929; ag. dir., crim. intell., 1932-36; supt., pol., 1933; divnl. supt., pol., 1936.

SCRIMGEOUR, COLIN GRAHAM.—B. 1903; ed. Gisborne pol. schl., N.Z.; home-missioner, Methodist Ch., 1923; city missioner, Auckland, 1926-32; dir., Friendly Road broadcasting statn., 1932-36; contrlr., N.Z. comm. broadcasting serv., 1936.

SCRIVENER, RUPERT FREDERICK.—B. 1890; assoc., R. Schl. of Mines, dipl., Imp. Coll. Science, assoc., I.M.M., assoc., Inst. of Mining and Metallurgy; survey work, England and Alaska, 1911-14; comand. serv., 1914-20; capt., 1918; served in Gallipoli, Egypt, Mesopotamia, India and Palestine; commanded, 29th Rly. Coy., Sappers and Miners, I.A.; asst. ch. engnr., Palestine rlys., 1920; engnr., ways and wks., Palestine rlys. 1924.

SCRIVENER, T. V.—B. 1908; ed. King's Schl., Canterbury and Oriel Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1930; apptd. temp. asst. prin., C.O., Oct., 1930; dist. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1933; ass't. dist. offr., Palestine, 1937.

SCUPHAM, MAJOR WILLIAM ERIC HALSTEAD, M.C.—B. 1893; ed. St. Paul's Schl.; army, 1914-19; dipl., anthropology, Cambridge, 1926; asst. polit. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Jan., 1920; dist. offr., Mar., 1931; dep. prov. comar., Jan., 1934; prov. comar., Oct., 1936; senr. prov. comar., Dec., 1937; ag. dep. ch. sec., 1936 and 1937; adminis. sec., 1939.

SCULLIN, RT. HON. JAMES HENRY, P.C.—El. to Commonwealth H. of R. for Corangamite, Victoria, 1910; defeated, gen. el., 1913; M.H.R. for Yarra, Victoria, since 1922; prime min. of the C'wealth of Australia, 1929-31.

SCULLY, HUGH DAY.—B. 1883; ed. pvte. and pub. schls. and Parkdale Collegiate Inst., Toronto, Univ., of Toronto; 1st cls. hons. and gold med. in polit. sc. and Alexander MacKenzie fellowship, 1906; commr., excise, Canada, 1932; commr., cust., 1933.

SEAGER, BASIL WILLIAM, O.B.E. (1939).—B. 1898; ed. abroad; mil'y. serv., 1916-22; Br. pro-consul, Jedda, Saudi Arabia, (Br. agency and consulate, later Br. Legn.), 1926-33; lent to Aden govt. as temp. polit. offr., during Anglo-Yemeni treaty negotiations, 1933-34; reverted to Jedda as Br. pro-consul, Mar.-Aug., 1934; polit. offr., Aden, Sept., 1934; ag. polit. sec. for various periods in 1935-39.
SEAGOE, ERNEST GOLDPINCH, M.B.E.—B. 1886; clk. to res. comsnr., New Hebrides, 1902; inspr. of native labourers, Br. residency, New Hebrides, 1909; ag. ast. to res. comsnr., 1911-12 and 1915-16; joint ag. nat. advocate, Oct., 1915, to Dec., 1922; ag. ast. to res., Nov., 1919 to Feb., 1920 and Sept. to Dec., 1921; commdt., constab., Aug., 1922; dep. comsnr., W. Pacific (New Hebrides), Nov., 1922; in ch. of accts., May to Aug., 1923; ag. ast. to res. comsnr., on various occasions, 1923-39; dist. agt. and lab. inspr., Apr., 1923; agt. dist. dist. and commdt., pol. (Br. div.), Apr., 1925.

SEARLE, Lancelot Alhan.—B. 1915; pol. probnr., Hong Kong, 1936; ast. supt., 1938.

SEDGWICK, P. C. M.—B. 1911; ed. St. Lawrence Coll., Ramsgate, Brasenose Coll., Oxford and Queen's Coll., Cambridge; cadet, Hong Kong, Sept., 1934; passed Cantonese, 1937; 3rd ast. col. sec., Aug., 1937; admstve. ast., urban coun., Sept., 1937.

SEDGWICK, RICHARD ROMNEY.—B. 1894; ed. Westminster and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; schol., Trinity Coll., 1912; 1st cls. hist. tripods, pt. I, 1914 and pt. II, 1915; Gladstone prize, 1914; elected fellow of Trinity Coll., 1919; M.A., 1919; appd. under reconstruction scheme ast. prin., Min. of Labour, 1919; ast. prin., C.O., 1922; pvt. sec. to parly. under sec. of State, D.O., 23rd Sept., 1929; prin., D.O., 1st Oct., 1930; offl. sec. to high comsnr. for U.K. in Australia, Sept., 1938.

SEED, CHARLES WILLIAM STANLEY.—B. 1898; ed. St. John's (R.C.) Coll., Wonesh, Surrey; Artists' Rifles, 1916; 2nd lieut., 12th London Regt., 1917; served in France, 1918-19; (G.S. and Victory Meds.); col. audit dept., July, 1921; ast. audr., Nigeria, Sept., 1921; ast. audr., Nyasaland, Dec., 1926; ag. senr. ast. audr., in 1927, 1928 and 1929; audr., Seychelles and Somaliland, July, 1930; also pvt. sec. to gov., Seychelles, 1931-33 and to O.A.G., July-Sept., 1933; senr. ast. audr., S.S. and F.M.S., 1936; ag. dep. audr., Nov., 1936.

SEEL, GEORGE FREDERICK.—B. 1895; ed. Macclesfield Grammar Schol. and Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford (schol.); on mily. serv., Cheshire Regt. in Gallipoli, Egypt and Palestine; appd. to air minv., 28th July, 1919; seconded for serv. in C.O., as ast. prin., 9th Jan., 1922; pvt. sec. to parly. under secy. of state for the cols. (Mr. Wm. Lunn, M.P.), 10th June 1929; prin., 17th Sept., 1929; sec., Rhodesia-Nyasaland R. Coms., 1938-39; ag. ast. sec., C.O., 3rd Nov., 1939.

SEHEULT, JOSEPH EMANUEL.—B. 1881; ed. St. Mary's Coll., Trinidad; entd. civ. serv., Trinid. Mar., 1902; ch. clk., dept. of agric., Jan., 1916; ast. censor, 1914; censor, Apr., 1918; man.-sec., agric. bank, Jan., 1928; sec., cocoa industry relief comtee., 1930; sec., agric. industry relief comtee., 1933; sec., cocoa subsidy bd., 1936.

SEHEULT, LEO GABRIEL, A.C.G.I., A.M. Inst. C.E.—B. 1886; ast. dist. offr., pub. works, Trinidad, Mar., 1911; 2nd grade dist. offr., Sept., 1916; 1st grade dist. offr., June, 1917; gen. ast. to ast. D.P.W., Jan., 1925; exec. engnr., July, 1930; divnl. engnr., Jan., 1936.

SEBORNE, 2nd EARL OF (creat. 1882), VISCOUNT WOLMER, BARON SELBORNE (U.K.), K.G. (1909), P.C. (1900), G.C.M.G. (1905), THE RT. HON. WM. WALDEGRAVE PALMER.—B. 1839; ed. at Winchester and at Univ. Coll., Oxford; B.A. (1st cls. hist.), 1882; ast. priv. sec. to Mr. Childers, Chanc. of Excheq., 1882-85; was mem. of parlmt. for E. Hants, 1885-92, and for W. Edinburgh City, 1892-95; succeeded his father, 1895; Under S. of S. for Cols., June, 1895; chmn., Pacific cable comtee., 1896; mem. of Pacific cable comtee., 1899; first lord of the admiralty, Nov. 12th, 1900; high comsnr. for S. Africa, and gov. and commdr.-in-chief of Transvaal and O.R.C., 1905 to 1910; ceased to be gov. of O.R.C. on grant of resp. govt., June, 1907; pres. of bd. of agric. and fisheries, 1915-16.

SMITH, REGINALD HOPKINSON, O.B.E. (1935).—B. 1898; ed. Chatham House, Ramsgate; served in the Royal Naval Divn., Oct. to Dec., 1914; H.A.C., Oct., 1915 to Oct., 1917; Indian Army R. of O., Nov., 1917 to Aug., 1919; Aden Field Force, July, 1918 to July, 1919; dist. pol. offr., Somaliland, July, 1919; dist. offr., Jan., 1931.

SMITH, ROBERT KNOWLTON, LL.B., K.C.—B. 1887; ed. St. Francois Xavier Univ., Antigonish, N.S.; grad. Dalhousie Law Schl.; admitted to Nova Scotia bar, Mar. 1911; K.C., Jan., 1929; crown pros., Cumberland County, N.S. Aug.-Oct., 1929; mayor, Amherst, 1923; el. to H. of C., Canada, Oct., 1925, re-elec. at g.e., 1926 and 1930; dep. min. of marine, Aug., 1935.

SMITH, TRAFFORD, M.A.—B. 1912; ed. City Boys Schl., Leicester and Trinity Coll., Cambridge, 1930-34 (state schl., senr. asbl., Jeston Exhibr.); B.A., 1933 (1st cls. pts. SMITH, WILLIAM FORGAN, M.L.A. (Queensland).—B. and ed. in Scotland; M.L.A., Queensland since 1915; successively min. without portfolio, sec. for pub. wks. and sec. for agr. and stock; premier and treas., June, 1932.

SMITH, WILLIAM HARDEN, B.A., M.B., B.Ch., B.A.O. (T.C.D.), L.M. (Rot.), D.P.H. (R.C.P. and S.I.), D.T.M. (Calcutta).—Ed. Trinity Coll., Dublin; surg. sub-liet., R.N.V.R., 1918; med. offr., Zanzibar, Nov., 1923; ag. D.D.S., on various occasions, 1930-33; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1935; do., Kenya, 1939.

SMITH-FOLLETT, ROBERT REDVERS, B.Sc., A.R.C.S.—B. 1901; ed. Skinners Schl. and Impl. Coll. Sci. and Tech. (B.sc. hons. chem.); Impl. Col. Trop. Agr., Trinidad, 1925; research asst. to prof., chem. and soil sci., 1927; chemist-ecologist att'd. to col. comtes., Br. Guiana, 1929; chemist-ecologist (dept. agr.), Br. Guiana, 1930.

SMUTS, GEN. THE RIGHT HON. J. C., P.C. (1917), C.H., K.C.—B. 1870; ed. at Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch; B.A., Cape Univ., 1891; Eben scholar at Christ's Coll., Camb.; double first in law tripods, 1894; barrister, Cape Col.; state-attorney, S. African Republic, 1898; served with Boer forces during S. African war, and was in comd. of Boer forces in Cape Col. during the latter part of the campaign; mem. of head comte. of Het Volk; col. sec., Transvaal, 1907; mem. of Imp. Conf. on Naval and Military Defence, 1909; min. of finance and defence, Union of S. Africa, 1912; min. of defence, 1915; in command of troops in E. Africa, 1916; mem. of British war cabinet; represented S. Africa at peace confce. at Paris, 1919; prime min. and min. of native affrs., Union of S. Africa, 1919-24; M.P. for Standerton, 1924; leader, opposition, 1924-33; pres., Br. Assn. for Advancement of Science, 1931; min. of just. and dep. prime min.
SMYLY, Sir Philip Crampton, K.T. Bach. (1905).—B. 1886; ed. at Trinity Coll., Dub., B.A., LL.B.; called to the bar, King's Inn, Dub., 1888; LL.D., 1891; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 1902; Queen's advocate, S. Leone, 1895; atty.-gen., 1896; ch. just., S. Leone, 1901; ch. just., Gold Coast, 1911; ret., 1929.

SNEATH, Paul Alfred Turner, M.B. (Toronto), M.C.P. & S. (Ontario), Cert. London S.T.M., D.P.H. (Toronto), M.D. (Toronto).—B. 1898; med. offr., W.A.M.S. (Gold Coast), 1923; resigned, 1927; prov. lieut., Canadian army medical corps, 1927; lieut., 1928; capt., 1929; Canadian O.T.C. (Toronto contingent), major (med.), R.C.A.M.C.(N.P.), 1931; asst. gov't. M.O.H., Br. Guiana, 1937; dep. dir., med. services, 1939.

SNELLING, Arthur Wendell.—B. 1914; ed. Ackworth Schol. and Univ. Coll., London; B.Sc. (economics) 1st, ola., hon., 1934; study group sec., Royal Inst. of Internat. Affairs., 1934-36; appl. after compet. exam., asst. prin., D.O., Oct., 1936.

SNYMAN, Nicolaas.—Prof. asst. to survr.-gen., O.F.S., 1920; survr.-gen., O.F.S., Dec., 1931; ditto, Natal, May, 1934; do., Transvaal, Dec., 1937; chmn., survr. bd., Dec., 1939.

SOERTSZ, Francia Joseph, K.C., Barrister-at-Law (Gray's Inn).—B. 1886; held several appts. as pol. mag., crown coun., dist. judge and commr. of assize, Ceylon, 1932-33; puisne just., Nov., 1936.

SOLLIS, Clifford George, M.A.—B. 1895; ed. Bristol Grammar Schol. and St. John's Coll., Oxford, asst. mast., Bukit Zahrah Schol., Johore Bahru, Dec., 1920; ag. inspr., schls., Pahang, Oct., 1925; do., Penang, Mar., 1928; supt., educn., Kedah, Dec., 1930; inspr., schls., Selangor, Aug., 1931; senr. inspr., Eng. schls., Hong Kong, 1937; J.P., 1937; dir. of educn., 1939; censor, 1939.

SOLOMON, Saul.—B. 1875; ed. Bedford Grammar Schol. and Lincoln Coll., Oxford; M.A.; called to bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1900; K.C., Union of S. Africa, 1919; judge, sup. ct., Transvaal prov. divn., 1927.

SOMASUNTHARAM, Kandiah.—B. 1897; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1921; attd., Kalutara kach., Dec., 1921; ditto, Kurunegala kach., Jan., 1922; ditto, Colombo kach., Dec., 1922; office asst. to rubber contr., Mar., 1923; office asst., Galle kach., Aug., 1926; 5th asst. col. sec., Nov., 1926; 4th asst. col. sec., May, 1928; admnl. asst. govt. agt., Colombo, Jan., 1929; admnl. asst. contr., rev., Nov., 1929; asst. govt. agt., Kurunegala, July, 1931; dist. judge, Kegalla, July, 1932; sec., min. for lab., industry and commerce, June, 1933; dep. contr., lab., May, 1934; contr., finance and supply, Jan., 1936.

SOMERS (6th Baron, cr. 1784), Arthur Herbert Somers Cocks, K.C.M.G. (1926), D.S.O. (1919), M.C. (1917).—B. 1887; ed. Charterhouse and New Coll., Oxford; serv. in Great War, 1914-19; capt., 1st Life Guards, 1914; lieut.-col., Tank Corps, 1918-19; ret., 1922; a lord in waiting in ordinary to the King, 1924; gov'r. of Victoria, 1926-31.

SOMERS, Cecil George.—B. 1896; served Dardanelles and E. Mediterranean with H.M. Transports, 1914-18; govt. pilot, Kenya, 1924; asst. port offr., Zanzibar, 1929; ag. port offr. on various occasions, 1929-37; asst. port and cust. offr., Jan., 1938; ag. port offr., Mar., 1938; port and cust. offr., Sept. 1938; ag. senr. cust. offr., June, 1939; lt.-comdr., Zanzibar Volunteer Force, Aug., 1939.

SOPER, Major Edward Joseph, (R. of O.), V.D.—B. 1889; engng. acct., F.M.S. Rly., Sept., 1923; asst. acct., Jan., 1925 and June, 1931; fincl. offr., engng. dept., July, 1928; do., gr. I, Sept., 1928; rev. acctnt., Aug., 1935.

SOPER, John Robert Philpott, B.A. (hons.), Cantab.—B. 1904; ed. Tonbridge Schol. and Pembroke Coll., Cambridge (schol.); headmaster, agrl. prim. schl., Zanzibar, Sept., 1926; seconded for duty as agrl. offr., 1926; agrl. offr., 1928; do., S.S. and F.M.S., 1936.

SOUTHALL, Colin Lambert.—B. 1898; ed. Sideot Schol.; R.F.C. 1915-19; B.S.C. (1st cls.) Birmingham; govt. chem., Fiji, 1921-28; asst. analyst, Straits Sttlmts., 1928; govt. analyst, Nigeria, 1936.

SOUTHBOROUGH, 1st Baron (creat. 1917), Rt. Hon. Sir Francis John Stephens Hopwood, P.C. (1912), G.C.B. (1916), G.C.M.G. (1908), K.C.B. (1901), K.C.M.G. (1906), C.B. (1895), C.M.G. (1893).—B. 1860; ed. at Louth by Canon W.W. Hopwood; admitted a solr., 1882; asst. law clk., B. of T., 1885-1888; asst. solr., 1888-1892; priv. sec. to pres. of B. of T., 1892; sec., rly. dept., 1892-1901; perm. sec., 1901; perm. under-sec. of S. for the colonies, 1907-1910; employed on different occasions upon offl. missions to U.S.A., Canada, and Newfoundland; Brit. deleg. to internat. rly. congress in London, 1895; and in Paris, 1900; hon. sec. to chmn. of select comte. of H. of C. on Jameson raid, 1897; mem. of London traffic comte., 1903; visited S. Africa as mem. of Transvaal and O.R.C. constitutions comte., 1906; mem. of comte. on canals and waterways, 1906; and on ocean freights and shipping "rings," 1906; accompanied H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his visit to Quebec, 1908; mem. of Royal comte. on electoral reform, 1909; registr. of the Order of St. Michael and St. George, 1907-1909; sec. of the Order, 1909-1911; accompanied H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught on his visit to S. Africa in connection with the opening of the first parlmt. of the Union of S. Africa, 1910; vice-chmn. of the Development comte., 1910; specially apptd. to act as under sec. of state for the colonies during the period of the Imperial Conf., 1911; additional civil lord of the Admiralty, Jan., 1912; sec. to the Irish Convention, 1917.

SOUTHORN, Sir Wilfrid Thomas, K.C.M.G. (1938), K.B.E. (1933), C.M.G. (1927).—B. 1879; ed. Warwick Schol. and Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford (M.A.); hon. LL.D. Prov., May, 1905; dist. judge, Tangalla, Apr., 1907; landing survr. customs, Colombo, July, 1909; asst. govt. agt., Matale, Nov., 1911; priv. sec. to gov., Aug., 1914; dep. collr. of customs and landing survr., Colombo, Sept., 1915; 2nd asst. col. sec., Dec., 1919; prim. asst. col. sec., July, 1920; prim. collr., cust. and chmn., Colombo port comte., Dec., 1923; mem., leg. coun., 1923 and exec. coun., 1925; col. sec., Hong Kong, May, 1926; O.A.G., for various periods, 1927-35; gov. and commodr-in-ch., Gambia, Oct., 1936.

SPAFFORD, Harold Hamilton, B.A.—B. 1899; mily-serv., France, 1917-18; demob., 1921; inspr., schls., Gold Coast, Jan., 1928; senr. inspr., do., 1938.
SPARROW, Herbert Robert, A.M.I.E.E.,—B. 1889; asst. elec. engrnr., F.M.S., Mar., 1920; elec. engrnr., K. Lumpur, Sept., 1927; ag. dep. ch. elec. engrnr. and inspr. in addn., various periods, 1928-31; senr. elec. engrnr., Selangor, Sept., 1930; ag. advr., elec. Malay States, Mar. 1937; advr., do., 1938.

SPARROW, William Labaute.—B. 1904; ed. Trinity Coll., Dublin; pol. probationer, Oct., 1924; asst. supt., pol., Hong Kong, 1927; seconded to Weihaiwei as junr. dist. offr., Jan., 1928; passed in Mandarin and Cantonese; atttl. Punjab pol., 1931-2; passed in Urdu, 1932; supt., pol., 1936.

SPEED, Sir Edwin Arney, Kt. Bach.(1911).—M.A., LL.B.; B. 1869; ed. at Rugby, and Trin. Coll., Camb.; major scholar and senior exhibtnr., Rugby schl.; scholar and prizeman of Trin. Coli., Camb. 1st cls. class. tripes, 1890; 2nd cls. law tripes, Part I., 1891; called to the bar, Inner Temple, June, 1893; dist. comsrr., G. Coast, 1899; atty.-gen., Lagos, 1900; edited a revised edition of Lagos laws, 1901; has acted on numerous occasions as ch. just. and also as col. sec., from Jan., 1905, to Mar., 1906; atty.-gen., S. Nigeria, May, 1906; edited revised edtn. of laws of S. Nigeria, 1907; ch. just., N. Nigeria, 1908; retired.

SPEERS, R. C., M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.), D.T.M. (Liv.)—B. 1901; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1925.

SPENCE, John, C.M.G. (1936), B.A., LL.B., (Syd. Univ.)—B. 1878; mem. pub. serv. bd., 1924-28; chmn., N.S.W. budget comtee., 1928; chmn. N.S.W. taxation investgn. comtee., 1933-35; audr.-gen., N.S.W. and trustee, Australian museum since, 1928.

SPENCE, Louis Percival.—B. 1895; clk., treas., St. Vincent, 1914; 1st cls. rev. and port offr., 1919; ch. rev., excise and port offr., 1927; ch. inland rev. offr., 1936; ag. col. treas., collr., cust., etc. on several occasions, 1934-37; col. treas., collr. cust., etc., Jan., 1938; ag. admr. in 1938.

SPENDER, Hon. Percival Claude, K.C., M.P.—Enlisted A.I.F., Sept., 1918; mem., Warringah (N.S.W.), H. of R., C. of A., from Oct., 1937; assist. treas., Menzies miny., Apr., 1939; ag. treas., Nov., 1939.

SPICER, Rot Godfrey Bullen, C.M.G. (1934), M.C. (1918).—B. 1889; ed. Colet Court and St. Paul's; probationary asst. supt. pol., Ceylon, Nov., 1909; asst. supt., 1911; supt., 1915; on war serv., 1915-19; (lieut., The Carabiniers): wounded, Oct., 1918; returned to Ceylon pol., 1919; supt., grade I., 1923; commr. pol., Kenya, June, 1925; inspr.-gen., pol. and prisons, Palestine, 1930.

SPIFFER, John Wyatt, C.M.G. (1938), M.Inst.C.E.—B. 1878; ed. Wellington Schil. (Som.); served in engnr. dept., G.W.R., as pupil, survr., and draughtsman, new wks. asst. and divnl-engnr., 1896 to 1910; joined engnr. dept., Crown Agents, 1910; services lent to Miny. of Munitions, 1916; tech. adviser to dir., Munitions Overseas Transport, 1917; returned to C.A., 1919; dep. ch. engrnr., 1919; visited Ceylon, F.M.S. and S. Stiltns., 1920; ch. engrnr. (designs), 1922; visited Br. Guiana and Trinidad, 1922; acted for one year as gen. man., and ch. engrnr. rly., F.M.S., 1926.

SPOONER, Arthur Casswell.—B. 1906; ed. Epsom Coll.; cadet, Gold Coast, 1929; asst. dist. comsrr., 1930.

SPOWERS, James Howaud.—B. 1889; authorised survr., Queensland, Oct., 1911; survr., F.M.S., Nov., 1913; asst. supt., surveys, Jan., 1919; do., trig. surveys, F.M.S., Nov., 1922; do., rev. surveys, Sept., 1924; ag. supt., surveys, Johohe, Jan., 1931; do., Kedah, Oct., 1932; supt., surveys, F.M.S. and S.S., June, 1933; do., rev. surveys, Selangor and N. SPRAGUE, William, A.M.I.N.A.—B. 1901; asst. govt. marine survr., Hong Kong, 1929.

SPURLING, Antony Cuthbert, M.A. (Oxon.), Barrister-at-Law (Inner Temple).—B. 1906; asst. legal advr., Miny. of Health, 1934; res. mag., Kenya, 1936; crown couns., 1939.

SQUIBBES, Francis Leopold.—B. 1895; ed. Towcester Schil.; served Manchester Rgt., 1914-19; Imp. war graves comm., 1920-22; entd. SRIKHANTA, Mayilvakanam, B.A. (Lond.).—B. 1913; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Jan., 1937; office asst., Putalam, Aug., 1938.

STACPOOLLE, George Wentworth.—Asst. comsrr., lands survey dept., Gold Coast, 1925; transf'd. to lands dept., 1927; ag. dep. comsrr., July, 1928-Apr., 1929; ag. comsrr., lands, in 1932 and 1933; comsrr., lands, Oct., 1933.

STACEY, Herbert Edward, Barrister-at-Law (Gray's Inn).—B. 1902; cler. serv., secre., Kenya, 1926; legal dept., 1928; ch. elk., 1936; legal asst., 1938; called to bar, 1939; ag. crown couns., 1939.

STACY-MARKS, Lieut.-Commdr. N.J., R.D., R.N.R.—B. 1893; ed. H.M.S. "Worcester"; served R.N., 1914-20; demob., 1920; 2nd offr., lake steamers, K.U.R. & H., 1920; asst. to port man., Mombasa, 1928; port man., 1933.

STAFFORD, Frank Edmund O.B.E. (1934).—Active serv. with Queen's Regt., 1914-19; Ira. civ. admtrm., Feb., 1919; asst. finan. advr., 1921; dep. finan. secy., Jan., 1923; finan. sec., 1923; ass't. treas., Nigeria, 1936; senr. asst. sec., 1937; ag. pr n. asst. sec., 1937; prin. asst. sec. (finance br.), 1938; ag. dep. finan. sec., 1939.

STALLARD, Charles Frampton.—B. 1871; ed. St. Edward's Schil. and Merton Coll., Oxford; Grays Inn (Holt schil.); called to bar, 1895; S. African War, 1900-02; advoc., Union of S. Africa; K.C., 1910; prov. coun., Transvaal, 1910-13; Great War, S.W. Africa, 1914-16, Flanders and Italy, 1916-18 (D.S.O., M.C., ment. in desps. three times); lieut.-col.: M.P. for Roodepoort, 1929-38; Pietermaritzburg, 1939; min. of mines, 1939.

STANHOPE, Reginald Alfred Browning, B.V. Sc. (Melb.), M.R.C.V.S., Melb. Univ. and Royal Vet. Coll., Lond.—B. 1891; vet. surg., F.M.S., May, 1920; ag. dir., vety. reach. and vety. advr., Malaya, July, 1936.

STANLEY, Sir Herbert James, G.C.M.G. (1930), K.C.M.G. (1924), C.M.G. (1913).—B.1872; ed. at Eton and Balliol Coll. Oxford (M.A.); priv. sec. to H.M. min. resident at Dresden and Coburg, and British vice-consul at Dresden, 1871-1902; asst. priv. sec. to first Lord of the Admiralty, 1906-1908; priv. sec. to Lord Pres. of the Com., 1908-1910; priv. sec. to Viscount Gladstone, gen. of Union of S. Africa, 1910; sec. to gov-.
gen., 1913; resident commr., Southern and Northern Rhodesia, 1st Apr., 1915; Imperial sec. and acctnt. to high commr. for S. Africa, 1918; first gov. and commdr.-in-chief, N. Rhodesia, 1st Apr., 1924; gov. of Ceylon, Aug., 1927; H. M. high commr. for S. Africa, and first high commr. for the U.K. in the Union of S. Africa, Apr., 1931; gov. and commdr.-in-ch., S. Rhodesia, 8th Jan., 1935.

STANLEY, ROBERT CHRISTOPHER STAFFORD.—B. 1899; ed. Westminster Schol. and R.M.A., Woolwich; R.G.A., 1918-21; on war serv., Palestine, 1918; admnstr. offr., Nigeria, May, 1925; do.; Cyprus: asst. sec., Dec., 1935; commr., Mar., 1936; ch. asst. sec., Mar., 1938; ag. col. sec., various periods, 1938-39; public informn. offr., Sept., 1939.

STANLEY, W. B., C.M.G. (1923), M.B.E. (1918), Barrister-at-Law, Gray's Inn, 1921.—Served with 1st bdr regt. occupation of Crete, 1898; S. Africa, 1899-1900 (med. and 4 clasps); 2nd lieut., W. Leone, 1910; prov. commr., May, 1920; ag. col. sec., S. Leone, on various occasions, 1918-20 and 1922-23; gov.'s dep. on several occasions.

STAPLES, JAMES WEBSTER.—B. 1902; apptd. after compet. exam., asst. clk., G.P.O., Oct., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; transf'd to C.O., Mar., 1923; ag. cler. offr., higher grade, 23rd Nov., 1939.

STAPLES, RAYMOND RHODES.—B. 1897; M.A. dip. agr. (Cantab.); botanist, Union of S.A., 1922; agr. economist, Tanganyika Territory, 1929; ag. dep. dir., agr., 1930; res. offr. (pasture, vety. dept.), 1931; botanist, 1935; ecological survy., Basutoland, 1937.

STAPLEY, FRANK R.—B. 1895; mily. serv., Sept., 1914 to Dec., 1919; temp. clk., C.O., Apr., 1920; apptd. cler. offr., 4th July, 1922; higher grade cler. offr., 17th Feb., 1930.

STATHAM, HON. SIR CHARLES ERNEST, KT. BACH. (1926).—Mem., N.Z. H. of R., 1915-35; speaker, 1923-35; M.L.C., 1936.

STEAD, KINGSLEY WILLANS, C.B.E. (1933), O.B.E. STEAD, ROBERT J. C.—B. 1880; asst. gen. publicity agt., colonization dept., C.P.R., 1913; gen. publicity agt., colonization dept., C.P.R., 1917; dir. publicity, dept. of immgr. and colonization, Ottawa, 1919; has written several books.

STEED, L. F.—B. 1897; on mily. serv., Sept., 1914 to Mar., 1919; temp. clk., O.S.O., Feb., 1920, apptd. after compet. exam., clerk., offr., O.S.O., July, 1922.

STEED, ROGER HERBERT, M.I.C.E., Chtd.civ. engrn.—B. 1894; ed Dulwich Coll.; war serv., 1915-19; asst. engtn., P.W.D., Malaya, Feb., 1924; supt., stores & furniture, S'pore, Oct., 1926; ag. ex. engrn., S'pore, Nov., 1929; ex., engrn., S'pore, Feb., 1933; ag. senr. ex. engrn., hdgtrs., Jan., 1933.

STEELE, Lieut.-Commr. ARTHUR DAVENY, R.N.R. (Retd.).—B. 1893; ed. Vale Coll., Rams-gate; cadet H.M.S. CHAPTER L—APPLICATION OF THE REGULATIONS.
